summary.name: Synthwave. Supplemental design reference, not a directly named style in the source collection; related to but not interchangeable with Retrofuturism.
summary.visualIdentity: 1980s electronic-music imagery: neon night colors, perspective grids, striped sunsets, and selected mountains or sports-car silhouettes. Magenta, cyan and warm orange separate against deep blue-purple. Optional VHS texture adds tape noise, tracking errors and color bleed without persistent corruption.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: horizon-drive imagery alone suits this style, and music videos, lyric visualizers and retro event promos benefit from section-synchronized drive. Inferred: video and interactive HTML both fit, with interactive delivery using an audio-linked WebGL scene. Titles may need a hybrid partner for typographic control.
summary.limitations: Avoid layering vaporwave or cyberpunk aesthetics, which blur its identity. Avoid flashing on every beat and persistent VHS corruption. CRT scanlines alone do not represent VHS artifacts. Visual details were user-guided and not verified against the source video. Duration, aspect ratio and resolution are unspecified.
summary.palette: Background policy is scene-dependent, so #171333 is an illustrative swatch, not a required canvas color. Suggested tokens are foreground #F8ECDC and accents #E05AAA, #5DCEE0, #EEA15D; no approved exact colors were supplied. The sunset gradient is optional, limited to sky and atmosphere. Two-color ratios such as 15.308:1 do not replace composited-frame checks.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Motion derives from composition time, with a clear horizon moving in sync with musical sections. Grid lines and silhouettes stay discrete. Interactive HTML may use keyboard controls and reduced-motion, but must seek deterministically. Motion references 037, 038 and 039 are optional, only if scene assets contain the matching phrase, punctuation or approved mark. References 012 and 015 are scroll-storytelling patterns.
summary.audio: The source mandates no audio layer, genre, tempo or voice. Music-driven sections are the core suggestion, with visual changes landing on verified beats only after actual audio inspection. No audio assets were supplied, and none were created. Any speech must remain intelligible over music. Tempo range is unspecified.
summary.assetRequirements: No uploads, exact copy, duration or frame rate were specified. Build needs local fonts, SVG or DOM text, and generated geometry for grids, roads, vehicles and sky. Mountains or car silhouettes are optional. Motion 037–039 need real phrase, punctuation or mark assets before use. Real audio is needed for any beat-synchronized timing.
summary.combinations: Style-105 adds section-synchronized horizon, grid speed and cut timing for music videos and event promos, driving Three.js grid speed and GLSL sunset stripes. Style-093 adds title and lyric typography in #F8ECDC with beat-landing outlines. Rules: keep the gradient in the sunset, keep grid lines discrete, and avoid text over the sun's brightest area.
summary.productionApproach: Style renderer: WebGL/GLSL and Three.js for roads, grids, vehicles and sunset sky, with SVG or DOM text. Separate seeded passes handle tape noise, tracking offsets and color bleed. Motion engine: one paused GSAP timeline, with Motion optional. Pipeline: HyperFrames by default, Remotion only with a recorded reason. chroma-js validates colors. Verify direct, backward and forward seeks.
